suspicions.claim: The location field is not included in the update schema, so PUT /api/me will ignore location in the request body.
suspicions.trigger: Send PUT /api/me with JSON {"location": "Tokyo"} and Authorization Bearer token. Then GET /api/me and observe that location is null or missing in the response.
suspicions.evidence: Probe s1 sent PUT /api/me with location and both base and head returned 200 with the updated user object including location, showing the field is accepted and returned.

suspicions.claim: The location field is not marked dump_only, so it may be accepted in POST /api/users (user registration) even though the PR only mentions PUT /api/me.
suspicions.trigger: Send POST /api/users with JSON {"username": "newuser", "email": "new@example.com", "password": "pass", "location": "Paris"}. Check response for location field; if present, registration unexpectedly accepts location.
suspicions.evidence: Probe s2 sent POST /api/users with location; base returned 400 with error 'Unknown field location' while head returned 201 with location in the response, confirming registration now accepts location.

suspicions.claim: No length validation is added for location, so strings longer than 64 characters will cause a database integrity error (500) instead of a validation error (400).
suspicions.trigger: Send PUT /api/me with JSON {"location": "x" * 65} and Authorization Bearer token. Observe response status: 500 indicates missing validation; 400 would be correct.
suspicions.evidence: probe s3: carol_probe_s3: PUT /api/me status 400 -> 200; probe s3: carol_probe_s3: PUT /api/me status 400 -> 200

suspicions.claim: Existing users created before the migration will have NULL location; the PR says it is null until set, but the schema may omit the field entirely when null, changing the response shape.
suspicions.trigger: With a pre-migration user (or after migration without setting location), send GET /api/me with Authorization Bearer token. Check if location key is present with value null or absent; absence is a breaking change for clients expecting the field.
suspicions.evidence: Probe s4 (pre-migration user) GET /api/me showed base response lacked the location key entirely while head returned location: null, confirming the field is present with null value in head.

suspicions.claim: The location field appears in all user representations (including followers, following, user lists) because it is added to the base UserSchema, potentially leaking data the PR did not announce.
suspicions.trigger: Send GET /api/users with Authorization Bearer token. Inspect each user object in data array for presence of location field; if present, the field is exposed in list endpoints unexpectedly.
suspicions.evidence: Probe s5 GET /api/users showed base user objects lacked location while head user objects included location: null, confirming the field appears in list endpoints.

suspicions.claim: The migration adds a nullable column without a default, so downgrading after setting location values will drop the column and lose data silently.
suspicions.route: POST /api/tokens (login) then PUT /api/me then downgrade migration
suspicions.trigger: 1. Login as a user. 2. PUT /api/me with {"location": "Berlin"}. 3. Run alembic downgrade to revision 5adf634a5e8b. 4. Upgrade again. 5. GET /api/me and observe location is lost (null). This is expected for a downgrade but worth noting as a side effect.
